text:
elaine: Heads up — canary CI shows p99 jump from 95ms -> 205ms after today's release. Looks like a serving runtime regression. Anyone oncall to run a bisect?

raj: saw it too. failing job: buildkite/run-perf-canary#842. attaching perf artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/perf/842/perf.tgz

micah: preliminary flamegraph points at select_kernel_for_batch and kv_cache::lookup_hot_prefix getting heavy.

samir: ack. can repro locally on my devbox with docker image: ghcr.io/redwood/inference:canary-2026-03-17

elaine: plan: git bisect between v2026-03-10 (good) and HEAD (bad). use microbench harness: tools/perf/run_microbench.py --suite=latency_p99 --iters=50

olga: FYI I noticed a heuristics change in kernel-selector that landed in a chain earlier today. commit range I suspect: 3b4f2a7..9f1d3c2

raj: can someone run git bisect with an automated test script? I can remote into samir's box but prefer someone with local gpu access.

samir: I can run it. steps I'm going to run:
```
git fetch origin
git bisect start HEAD v2026-03-10
git bisect run ./tools/perf/bisect_runner.sh --bench latency_p99 --target 100
```
I'll post results in ~45m.

ci-bot: buildkite:perf-canary #842 failed — logs at https://buildkite/redwood/842

micah: quick hypothesis: KV cache pruning changed LRU weights last week; might cause more cache misses and increased kernel selection work. If bisect hits a KV-related commit, that would line up.

elaine: good hypothesis. if bisect points to kv commit we should rollback that patch from canary and re-run canary.

samir: running now. I added extra logging to bisect_runner to capture per-call time for select_kernel_for_batch.

raj: ping @samir — if bisect is slow we can narrow by testing only the commits that touch runtime/kernel_selector.{cc,h}

samir: update: bisect hit a bad commit: 9f1d3c2 (heuristics: normalize batch score for kernel selection). Profiling snippet:
```
select_kernel_for_batch  total_ms=1234  (+420% vs good)
kv_cache::lookup_hot_prefix total_ms=312  (+180% vs good)
```

olga: that's the heuristics normalization change I mentioned. looks like we changed normalization to be based on batch_size instead of effective_seq_len, causing suboptimal kernel picks for short sequences.

icah: can we revert that one-line change and re-run canary quickly? it's small.

elaine: yes please do a hotfix PR with revert + perf test. tag it release-critical. I'll block the rollout until canary is green.

raj: creating revert PR now: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/7145

ci-bot: build queued for PR 7145

samir: once CI for PR passes, I'll deploy to canary and run full perf suite. ETA ~30m after merge.

elaine: thanks all. great bisecting teamwork :thumbsup:

micah: note for postmortem: add targeted unit tests for kernel-selector normalization and a perf-gate for p99 on short sequences.

olga: logging ticket created: INF-2392

elaine: closing loop — will open a short postmortem after canary stable.
